checks.title: A dependency lockfile is committed
checks.why: Without a lockfile, production resolves versions independently of what was tested, so a deploy can install a release nobody has ever run. It is also how most dependency confusion attacks land.
checks.action: Commit exactly one lockfile for the package manager you use, and install from it in production with a frozen install rather than a fresh resolve.

verify.cmd: git ls-files package-lock.json yarn.lock pnpm-lock.yaml bun.lockb | head -5
verify.expect: Exactly one lockfile is listed. Zero means nothing is pinned, more than one means two package managers are fighting.

checks.title: The Node version is pinned for the deploy environment
checks.why: Hosts pick a default Node major when nothing declares one, and that default moves. A silent major bump can change TLS behaviour, crypto defaults and native module compatibility mid-deploy.
checks.action: Declare the Node version in the engines field of package.json, and mirror it in .nvmrc so local development matches production.

verify.expect: A version file exists, or package.json declares an engines field naming a Node major.

checks.title: Production installs omit dev dependencies
checks.why: Dev dependencies ship test fixtures, build tooling and their transitive trees to production. They enlarge the artifact and the attack surface without running a single line of application code.
checks.action: Install with the production or omit-dev flag in the deploy step, and confirm nothing at runtime imports a package listed under devDependencies.

verify.expect: The tree resolves with no missing packages, meaning the application runs without anything from devDependencies.

checks.title: Known vulnerabilities in production dependencies have been reviewed
checks.why: Most JavaScript projects carry hundreds of transitive packages. An advisory in one of them is the cheapest way into an application that is otherwise well written.
checks.action: Run an audit against production dependencies only, then either upgrade or record why each remaining advisory does not apply to how you use the package.

verify.expect: No high or critical advisories, or a written note explaining why each remaining one is not exploitable here.

checks.title: Source maps are not published to production
checks.why: A published source map hands anyone the original sources, including comments, internal endpoint names and any key that was inlined at build time. Browsers fetch them automatically when devtools is open.
checks.action: Disable source map emission for the production build, or upload maps to your error tracker as a private artifact instead of serving them.

verify.expect: No map files under a directory that gets deployed. Maps under a private build artifact are fine.
